page.layout: One text column of running text at top, with a marginal-free argument heading in the middle. Below the text, a bracketed tree diagram (synopsis of the Pythian games) occupies the full width, followed by the abbreviation "E.j." beneath it. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: qua bestiæ langorem deficientis iam & ad extrema sese conuertentis sibila morientisque exprimebantur. Græca scholia aliquanto aliter constituunt partes: primam πνίγος[?] vocant, qua periculum certaminis cum serpente fiebat. 2. Iambum, propter conuicia quæ pertulerit Apollo ante certamen. 3. Δάκτυλον[?], propter Dionysium, qui primus oraculo præfuit. 4. κέλητον[?], propter Iouem. 5. μαντεῖον[?], propter terram: huius enim fuerat oraculum. 6. ἀνέρυγμα[?], propter serpentis sibilum. atque ad hunc modum Apollinem omnia constituisse aiunt.

Apud Romanos ludi hinc Apollinares instituti sunt, secundo bello Punico, de quorum origine vide Liuium Decad.3.lib.5. Hinc singulis annis à Prætore vrbis fiebant, eos populus coronatus spectabat. voti sunt primùm victoriæ ergò, non valetudinis causa, vt ex Liuij loco patet.
main_text.head: Argumentum breue Pythiorum.
main_text.p: CElebratur à Pindaro diuersi victores, qui diuersis temporibus in ludis Delphicis coronati sunt, idque ob diuersa exercitia, quibus excelluerunt. alij enim vicerunt.

page.notes: The Greek words in the numbered list (items 1, 3, 4, 5, 6) and the Greek label above "1." in the diagram are hard to read at this scan resolution; the marked readings are doubtful. The lines of the diagram are reconstructed from the brackets and their levels. The large initial "C" of "Celebratur" is joined to the following word as the drop cap.
